# Source ledger — literature audit wave 9

Only located sources are listed. Inspection level and native use are explicit.

## S80 — Dubickas: integer sequences generated by linear maps

**Record:** Artūras Dubickas, *On Integer Sequences Generated by Linear Maps*, Glasgow Mathematical Journal 51 (2009), 243–252. DOI `10.1017/S0017089508004655`.

**Inspected:** complete author-uploaded full text, including Theorems 1–3 and the ceiling-map remark.

**Located content:** bounded fixed integer linear observables of a floor/ceiling orbit are exactly multiples of the multiplier's minimal polynomial; the canonical rational-base digit word is not ultimately periodic; its factor complexity has an explicit linear lower bound.

**Native use:** `LIT-KTHM-0055`; exact external counterpart to PR #64/PR #66 finite linear and rational-section rigidity.

## S81 — Dubickas–Mossinghoff: Z-numbers and approximate multiplication

**Record:** Artūras Dubickas and Michael J. Mossinghoff, *Lower Bounds for Z-Numbers*, Mathematics of Computation 78 (2009), 1837–1851. DOI `10.1090/S0025-5718-09-02211-X`.

**Inspected:** complete author-uploaded full text, especially map (1.1), Proposition 3.1, Proposition 3.2, and the integer/fractional recurrence interface.

**Located content:** the partial map `x -> ceil(px/q)` on a proper residue set; singleton residue sets always terminate; universal termination implies explicit accumulation bounds and, when `p<|S|q`, nonexistence of `Z_(p/q)`-numbers.

**Native use:** `LIT-KTHM-0056`; exact identification of the PR #64 six-branch chart as one approximate-multiplication instance.

## S82 — Andrieu–Eliahou–Vivion: rational-base normality

**Record:** Mélodie Andrieu, Shalom Eliahou, and Léo Vivion, *A Normality Conjecture on Rational Base Number Systems*, arXiv `2510.11723`, version 2 dated 7 April 2026.

**Inspected:** complete accessible preprint, including Conjectures 1.3/1.6, Theorem 1.7, Question 3.15, Proposition 3.16, and Remark 3.17.

**Located content:** conjectural normality of every nonzero minimal word; equivalence with residue equidistribution of ceiling-map orbits; normality implies termination of every approximate-multiplication map; the termination question is equivalent to occurrence of every letter in every minimal word.

**Native use:** `LIT-KTHM-0057`; the six-branch chart needs only occurrence of the single digit zero, far less than full normality.

**Status caution:** preprint and conjectural at the load-bearing point.

## S83 — Matveev: explicit Archimedean logarithmic forms

**Record:** E. M. Matveev, *An Explicit Lower Bound for a Homogeneous Rational Linear Form in the Logarithms of Algebraic Numbers. II*, Izvestiya: Mathematics 64 (2000), 1217–1269. DOI `10.1070/IM2000v064n06ABEH000314`.

**Inspected:** official metadata and abstract; the complete English PDF was located but its theorem normalization was not inspected in this pass.

**Located content:** explicit exponential lower bounds for nonzero homogeneous linear forms in logarithms of algebraic numbers.

**Native use:** source requested for independent audit of PR #53/PR #70 all-repetition pulse cutoffs.

## S84 — de Weger: real and p-adic lattice reduction

**Record:** B. M. M. de Weger, *Solving Exponential Diophantine Equations Using Lattice Basis Reduction Algorithms*, Journal of Number Theory 26 (1987), 325–367. DOI `10.1016/0022-314X(87)90088-6`.

**Inspected:** official abstract and metadata.

**Located content:** effective algorithms for `S`-unit inequalities and equations using real and p-adic multidimensional approximation and lattice-basis reduction.

**Native use:** recommended second stage after a crude Matveev bound for fixed-support repetition equations in PR #53/PR #70.

## S85 — Chim: explicit two-term p-adic logarithms

**Record:** Kwok Chi Chim, *Lower Bounds for Linear Forms in Two p-adic Logarithms*, Journal of Number Theory 266 (2025), 295–349. DOI `10.1016/j.jnt.2024.07.012`.

**Inspected:** official abstract and metadata.

**Located content:** explicit bounds for `|alpha_1^b1-alpha_2^b2|_p`, with logarithmic dependence on the exponent height.

**Native use:** candidate for repetition equations retaining a two-term p-adic closeness condition after sparse-resultant elimination.

## S86 — Bugeaud: simultaneous m-adic logarithms

**Record:** Yann Bugeaud, *Linear Forms in Two m-adic Logarithms and Applications to Diophantine Problems*, Compositio Mathematica 132 (2002), 137–158. DOI `10.1023/A:1015825809661`.

**Inspected:** official abstract and metadata.

**Located content:** sharp explicit estimates simultaneously for several non-Archimedean valuations, with applications to fractional parts of rational powers.

**Native use:** possible mixed-prime strengthening of the pulse and centered-power height programs.

## S87 — Dubickas centered-power trilogy

**Records:**

1. Artūras Dubickas, *On the Distance from a Rational Power to the Nearest Integer*, Journal of Number Theory 117 (2006), 222–239. DOI `10.1016/j.jnt.2005.07.004`.
2. Artūras Dubickas, *On the Powers of 3/2 and Other Rational Numbers*, Mathematische Nachrichten 281 (2008), 951–958. DOI `10.1002/mana.200510651`.
3. Artūras Dubickas, *Powers of a Rational Number Modulo 1 Cannot Lie in a Small Interval*, Acta Arithmetica 137 (2009), 233–239.

**Inspected:** official abstracts and metadata only. Full theorem formulas and endpoint conventions were not acquired.

**Located content:** explicit large/small nearest-integer limit points, two-interval exclusions, and small-interval impossibility for rational powers.

**Native use:** highest-priority source acquisition for PR #16/PR #67 centered `81/64` ordinary-section work.

## S88 — Väänänen–Wallisser retained finite-dimensional firewall

**Record:** K. Väänänen and R. Wallisser, *A Linear Independence Measure for Certain p-adic Numbers*, Journal of Number Theory 39 (1991), 225–236.

**Inspected:** complete user-supplied PDF, including Theorem 1 and Padé determinant/remainder lemmas.

**Located content:** quantitative p-adic linear independence of finite vectors of Tschakaloff values in distinct multiplicative orbits under an explicit dimension-dependent condition.

**Native use:** retained for periodic and finite-dimensional prescribed controllers; not an ordinary-root extraction theorem.

## Cautions

- S82 is conjectural where normality or equidistribution is invoked.
- S83–S87 require full-PDF theorem inspection before exact native constants or hypotheses are promoted.
- Abstract-level logarithmic-form sources suggest an effective pipeline but do not automatically match a native pulse equation.
- None of these sources supplies a standard Collatz counterexample or a general ordinary-integer extraction theorem.
